body: And then what of the .eslintrc file in my home directory that I use as a default for projects that don't have one? I wouldn't want it merged if a project had its own config.

The merging behavior you describe (where the closest `.eslintrc` has overrides) is the way I intended this to work. If it's not doing that right now, then that's a bug. 

That said, I think everything having to do with configuration is a giant mess right now, and I'm not sure I want to dramatically change the behavior without taking the time to refactor configurations into something sane. I feel like adding more crap onto the pile will just make it all that much harder to deal with in the future.

Ah, that is quite small. That makes me less fearful.

I'd vote for 1 - I think it's more common to have project-specific .eslintrc files than it is to rely on home directory .eslintrc files. 

Do we currently search all the way to the home directory?

Currently, yes, it goes as far as it can.

There's a possible infinite loop in the above code, if you have an eslintrc file in your root directory, but that seems a bit edge case-y. I also wasn't sure what the behaviour of path.dirname is on windows when "c:\" is passed in.

issue.body:
Large projects often require many `.eslintrc` files for different globals/environments etc.; they often share most rules, though. jsHint for this specific use case has the `extend` option to which you pass a path to a different `.jshintrc` file. I think ESLint should add such a feature; it would also help in a migration from jsHint.

issue.body:
Found bugs on nested projects, when tryed to migrate 0.6.2 -> 0.7.3. Here is how to reproduce.

clone repo + install supbrojects (those are placed no node_modules) + install local & global eslint.

```
git clone https://github.com/nodeca/nodeca.git
cd nodeca
make pull-ro
npm install eslint@0.7.3
npm install -g eslint
```

if you have problems with `make`, then install one subproject manually:

```
mkdir node_modules
cd node_modules
git clone https://github.com/nodeca/nodeca.core.git
cd ..
```

---

**Bug 1** when running eslint from current dirs, parent dir configs are loaded. Current dir should be top point for hierarchy of configs.

```
cd ./node_modules/nodeca.core
eslint ./
```

It report, that can't find rule `no-lodash-aliases` definition. But this rule is defined and enabled on upper level, relative to current dir. Eslint should not scan dirs upward from current one.

---

**Bug 2** .eslintignore is merged improperly:

```
cd ./node_modules/nodeca-core
make lint
```

or from main project (nodeca) root:

```
eslint --rulesdir support/eslint_plugins/ ./node_modules/nodeca.core
```

Result: file `./node_modules/nodeca.core/.eslintignore` handled improperly, and eslint don't skip `assets/vendor` subfolder. That looks like hand for a long time. If you have a patience to wait - you will see lot of error about vendor libraries.

body:
I'm running into trouble with the merging behavior - a module A has a newer version of eslint with a new rule. it's dep is module B, which has an older version, and an eslintrc that doesn't have the new rule. In module A, `npm explore B npm run eslint` (where `npm run eslint` eslints my files), errors, because B's `eslint` is walking upwards and grabbing the incompatible eslint file from project A.

Is there a way I can disable the merging behavior, so that the first one found wins?
@ljharb why do you need to run ESLint on a dependent package? Shouldn't it be linted in its own repository?

@mzgol es7-shim's `npm test` runs the tests of all its dependents, and those dependents include linting as part of their tests.

But, it seems nonsensical that simply moving a directory elsewhere would change the output of a command that should be deterministic :-/ Creating `/.eslintrc` shouldn't have the ability to break eslint on every project on my computer.
